en: Yes. But my grandmother wanted to come to Japan while she was still healthy enough to make the trip. So that's why she's coming this year.
Someday she'll be too old to leave the house, so she asked us to set aside money to go and visit her when the time comes.
Your grandmother sounds nice. You'll need to take care of her as much as possible.
Indeed! I've been discussing with my mother quite a bit about where to take her.
Well, just because it's New Year's, don't make her eat stuff like mochi. I doubt foreigners are too familiar with traditional Japanese food.
Of course! You're so thoughtful, Shinada-san!
Give my regards to your mother!
You have to go see her, no matter what. I mean, you never know when something might happen, so you should make an effort to see each other while you still can.
I know that, of course. But still, it isn't quite that simple.
That's a tough situation. Going home takes money, and if you have money then that means you don't have time. And when you have time, your parents are already gone.
That is quite true. And that's why I want to see my grandmother as much as possible. It is very difficult when I'm not able to.
Geez, this is getting kinda depressing. Do you want to talk about something else?
That's just an excuse. People say that, and then let big opportunities slip through their fingers. Regret won't do anything to bring those back.
Yes, you're right, of course.
Perhaps I should talk to my mother about us going to France this year instead.
I think that's a great idea!
So are you half-Japanese?
Yes. My mother is French.
Hehe. This is my natural hair color, you know.
I'm so jealous! I bet guys go crazy over your blonde hair, huh?
Oh, not really. Lots of Japanese women dye their hair, after all. More often than not I get mistaken for a gyaru.
Oh, I get you. If a girl wears gaudy clothes and has blonde hair, I might make the same mistake.
That's why, personally, I feel somewhat jealous when I see people with lovely black hair.
You want what you can't have. I think everyone feels that way about certain things.
You don't look it. I would never have guessed if you didn't mention it.
They say many of us who are half-Western and half-Asian take on a more Asian appearance as we grow older.
That would be your dominant genetic traits. Does that mean you looked more French when you were little, Shion-chan?
Yes, my eyes were even blue back then. I looked like a little Western doll!
Really? I'd love to see pictures!
It's so easy to take pictures with a mobile phone these days, isn't it? Now I take pictures all the time!
What do you take pictures of?
If I see a moment I want to capture, I'll snap a picture of it. I get a lot of good shots on my way from home to work.
Street photography, huh? You must have a good aesthetic sense, eh?
I don't do that.
Oh? Why not?
Because I'm a professional journalist. I'm not some amateur who uploads pics of what he had for lunch to his blog.
A real photographer should strive to only take pictures that contain valuable information for his audience, and nothing else.
You sure do take pride in your photography. I can respect that!
Aw, it's not that big of a deal! Hehe.
What sort of photos do you take, Shinada-san?
I, uh, well... I take pictures of people.
Oh, you mean portraits? That sounds like it must be interesting!
Come to think of it, I don't think I've had my picture taken since my high school graduation.
You don't even have a photo at the club?
No, I don't. There would be problems if my photo got uploaded to the net.
That's right. Anyone can copy a picture and send it around, and who knows who'll see it?
Do you take pictures of yourself, Shinada-san?
I do. At PrintCircle photo booths.
Oh! I do that too!
Aren't photo booths these days amazing? You can make your eyes all big, or make your body all super-skinny and stuff. Haha.
Well, they include features meant to make girls look cuter. I imagine they're not suited for men.
But they're still fun to use. When you see the finished pictures, it's always a big surprise.
I don't. Unless it's for an ID or something.
Oh. You're rather good looking, so I imagine you're quite photogenic.
I do. Would you be willing to model for me? I enjoy photographing people from time to time.
Would I ever! I'd be absolutely okay with that!
Hehe. I've never taken nude photos of a man before. I'm a bit nervous!
Hold up, did you say nude!?
I, uh, just mean... Wouldn't you be better off with someone more suited to being photographed?
Oh, that's a shame. I've got such an interest in the naked male form.
...I think I made the right call.
What a waste. I bet you'd bring in a ton of clients if your photo was posted, Shion-chan.
Oh no, that wouldn't do. I don't want word getting out that I work here.
I guess that's that, then. Plenty of other girls don't post their photos either, I guess.
But with a stunning face like yours, Shion-chan, I bet your customers would take one look at you and have your image burned into their minds!
Oh my. That would be quite a sight!
I could take your picture if you want, Shion-chan.
You bet. How do you feel about nudes?
Are... Are you serious?
Of course! You'd make for a lovely subject!
That isn't the issue here.
Hey, you're still young. What's wrong with having photos from the prime of your life?
I suppose just once wouldn't hurt. And I bet someone like you would take lovely photos!
Now we're talking! A promise is a promise, okay?
That was a joke, sorry. I crossed the line.
Given that you're a professional, I'm sure it would be fine, but I'm rather shy.
Everyone is shy at first. Heck, some girls are fine with nudes, but refuse to show their face.
The other day, a friend of mine invited me to the track to watch a race.
That's unusual. Are you into that sort of thing?
My friend's boyfriend is an amateur racer. He was competing in the race with his own car, so we went to cheer him on.
How did he do?
Well, he struck another car partway through the race, so he had to drop out. Thankfully, his injuries were minor.
That's good. Considering the speeds those guys reach, it wouldn't be surprising if they got pretty badly hurt.
Quite so. When the accident happened, I had to turn away.
It must have been terrifying. Your friend must have been in tears, I'm guessing.
She actually looked fairly unconcerned. All she said was, "Aw, geez, not again."
She must be used to it. Still, newer cars are tough, so a little fender-bender probably isn't too bad.
Maybe so. If my boyfriend were in a race like that, I'd never be able to keep myself composed while I watched.
That's harsh. She should have shown at least a little concern for her boyfriend's well-being.
Indeed. She must have seen so many crashes that she's desensitized at this point.
I understand the thrill of taking risks, but it's somewhat barbaric to make it a spectator sport.
True that.
"Again"? You mean he crashes every time?
Yes! She said it's rare for him to even finish!
Wow, that guy sure is determined. I don't get what goes through rich people's heads.
I guess that's part of the thrill, though. Watching races wouldn't be terribly interesting if it weren't for the occasional nasty crash.
I do understand that line of thinking, but put yourself in the shoes of a worried onlooker. I prefer sports that are less harrying to watch.
I guess motorsports aren't for everyone.
Bet the repair bill's high. Any idea how much it came to?
Well, since it was an accident mid-race, involving a personally modified vehicle, insurance doesn't cover any of it.
Yikes. So he has to foot the whole bill himself?
It sounds like he's going to forego repairs and simply buy a new car. He said it's a good opportunity to purchase something different.
For real!? He must have more money than a pro! Doesn't even sound like a sport, really.
You reap what you sow. But I guess if you're going to race, you've got to be prepared for the potential expense.
Since he does it as a hobby, I believe money isn't an issue for him. Besides, the prize money wasn't very much anyways.
I see. If it's only a hobby, I guess that makes sense. I'm picky about my own equipment too.
Oh, so you and he are alike, then?
Hey, don't lump me in with him. I'm always trying to cut down on my living expenses.
When you say "not much", how much are we actually talking?
I believe first place was 3 million yen?
Holy cow! That much!?
Yeah, but that's not even enough to cover maintaining the vehicle. I suppose it'd be enough to prepare for the next race?
Wow, you guys sure live charmed lives.
Can you hold your liquor well, Shinada-san?
Sure. Though I should point out I haven't drunk a lot of the high-end stuff.
If you can drink regular alcohol, your tolerance is plenty high. People who can't hold their liquor can't even handle a single beer.
I guess? I come from a sports background, so I have a lot of experience with my teammates forcing me to drink a lot.
Oh my. If you were still okay with that, I suppose that means you had a natural tolerance.
Maybe. But I haven't done that in a while.
That means you can control how much you let yourself drink. I'm somewhat envious, to be honest.
What about you, Shion-chan?
Oh, I try not to drink alcohol, actually.
Can you drink?
Yes. I enjoy alcohol quite a bit, but for a while I wound up overdoing it. I was almost a borderline alcoholic.
So you can't drink?
No, I can hold my own. The problem was I kept drinking too much, and almost became an alcoholic.
Are you a mean drunk?
Of course not! I am a proper lady!
Actually, I suppose you weren't far off the mark, really. I'm emotionally unstable when I get drunk. I almost became borderline alcoholic.
No way! Really?
My doctor has forbidden me from drinking now, so I'm careful not to have even a tiny drop.
Is that so? In that case, I won't encourage you to drink, and if I think you've had too much, I'll be sure to stop you.
I'm sorry to put that sort of burden on you as my customer.
Oh, don't worry about it. Besides, it'll be cheaper for me.
You'll be okay. Since you're aware you can't drink too much, it should be easy for you to drink in moderation.
Another customer tried to tell me of the same thing, but I wound up drinking too much and had a relapse.
Please don't ask me to drink, okay?
Oh. Okay then, I'll watch myself.
C'mon, you must drink, right? You've been requesting drinks like business as usual.
Oh, those are just soft drinks. There isn't any alcohol in them.
For real!? But they're still expensive!
Well, the customer did order me alcohol, after all. Whether I'm served alcohol or not isn't really a problem.
And how is that not a scam?
On the other hand, if someone orders champagne, I have to pour the glasses out in the open, so I can't hide it. I have to just brace myself and drink.
I think I'll stop ordering you such expensive drinks from now on.
I couldn't allow alcohol to consume my life, which is how I was able to bring myself to stop before I developed an addiction.
Looks like your self-respect saved the day.
Indeed. I won't allow alcohol to get the better of me again.
Good call. Drinking should be enjoyed, but it shouldn't control you. You have to live a life that's not dependent on alcohol.
Oh, well said! I'll be sure to follow your example from now on, Shinada-san!
Haha. Well, the only reason why I don't drink every day is because I can't afford to.
Really? If you're serious about quitting alcohol, this job isn't for you.
Don't you think I know that already? But I can't get by without working, so I don't really have much of a choice.
I know full well that it isn't good for me, so please, spare me the lecture if you would.
Hey, I'm only thinking about your well-being.
There were a... number of unpleasant private matters going on at the time.
Drinking allowed me to feel good. Before I knew it, I was drinking from morning until night.
If my mother hadn't noticed and dragged me to the doctor, I may well have died from cirrhosis by now.
Wow. You should be grateful to your mother.
Yes. And so I strive never to trouble her like that again.
I've always liked the idea of living overseas. In fact, I only really watch movies and TV dramas from abroad.
They do seem more popular than Japanese ones, don't they? They've got a way bigger section at the video rental place, too.
